intro: Who can sign in to your organisation, what each person may see and do, and where. People hold a role at a place; a role is a set of permissions; groups and approval policies decide whose yes a document needs.
start: Look through Roles and see what each one can do, in plain words, before you invite anyone.
Invite your colleagues as the role that fits, at the places they work.
Make a group, such as the finance team, if several people should be able to approve.
Add an approval policy for the documents that must wait for a yes.

articles.title: Invite a colleague and choose what they may do
articles.summary: Send an invitation as a role at the places it applies to. They get an email to accept it and set their password.

steps.rest: one email address, or many at once. Everyone here is invited as the same role.

steps.lead: Choose what they will be able to do.
steps.rest: See what each role can do opens the roles beside it.
all places, or the ones they work at. Add another role gives them a second role somewhere else.
Nothing is sent until you press it. Anyone who could not be invited is listed, with why.

articles.after: They show on People as invited until they accept. An invitation lasts a week. Resend the invitation makes a new link and the old one stops working; Revoke the invitation stops it.
tips: Only an owner can make someone an owner, and an organisation always keeps at least one.
To change what someone holds later, open their row's Actions and press Open their access. Removing their last role takes them out of the organisation; their account stays.

articles.title: Change what a role may do
articles.summary: Open the role, switch on what it may see and change, and every person holding it gets the change.

steps.rest: on Roles. It says what it can see, change and approve, in plain words, and who holds it.
Or press New role, and start from a template or from nothing.
it should carry, area by area. Find a permission searches them all.
Someone already signed in sees the change after they sign in again.

tips: Give this role to someone here gives the role to a person at a place, from the role itself.
Compare roles sets two roles side by side.
A role that makes its holder an owner can only be changed by an owner.

articles.title: Make a document wait for someone's yes
articles.summary: An approval policy says which documents wait, when, and who approves them, in order. Without one, documents go straight through.

steps.lead: Name it and choose the kind of document,
steps.rest: such as quotations or supplier bills.
for example when its amount is over a figure, or only at one place. Leave it empty to cover every one.
Each step asks people, a role or a group, and says whether any one of them or all of them must agree.
if it needs one, and who else is asked when it passes.
Who would be asked shows who a document like this would wait for.

tips: A group gathers the people a policy can ask. Make one on Groups with New group; it gives nobody any permission.
Switching a policy off sends its documents straight through again. Those already waiting go on waiting until decided or withdrawn.
Try it: who would be asked? checks a kind of document, an amount and a place before any real document arrives.
